persona: High school strength coach recording sprint times during field testing, written down quickly
source_style: Hand-entered into CSV from field test clipboard notes, dates in mixed formats

columns.name: Name
columns.notes: Athlete names inconsistent (some nicknames, some initials, some full names; 2 rows blank)

columns.name: Date Tested
columns.notes: Three different date formats: MM/DD/YYYY, MM-DD-YY, DD-MM-YYYY

columns.name: 30m Sprint
columns.notes: Sprint time in seconds, header missing unit

columns.name: Agility T-Test
columns.notes: T-test time in seconds, header missing unit

columns.name: Notes
columns.notes: Field notes, mostly empty; includes remarks like 'Good form', 'Tired', 'check sheet'

clean_table.rows_note: athlete 6 missing name in original, rows 6 and 11 have blank athlete names

intended_analysis: For each athlete, did sprint times (10m and 30m) improve from test date 1 to test date 2? What is the relationship between 10m sprint time and T-test agility time?
mess_applied: Athlete names are inconsistent: some are nicknames (Marcus J., Derek T), some are full names, some are initials, and 2 rows are blank with notes asking who they are
Dates in three different formats: MM/DD/YYYY (09/14/2024), MM-DD-YY (09-14-24), and DD-MM-YYYY (14-09-2024)
30m Sprint and Agility T-Test column headers are missing units (should say '(s)' for seconds)
Missing athlete names in two rows (rows 6 and 11) with annotations in Notes column
Notes column has random observations mixed in (Good form, Tired, Wind?, check sheet) instead of being for actual notes
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: A parser might read dates in mixed formats as three different columns or fail entirely. Blank athlete names could cause row alignment to shift. The column headers don't specify units for two time-based columns, so a reader would need to infer they are seconds like the first one.
